newsitem.title: LEBANON: Italy and Lebanon condemn Israel's settlement work.
newsitem.headline: Italy and Lebanon condemn Israel's settlement work.

text.p: Prime Ministers of Italy and Lebanon condemned on Tuesday the beginning of work on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem, saying it has further complicated the logjammed regional peace talks.
Italy's Romano Prodi and Lebanon's Rafik al-Hariri were speaking at the end of Prodi's brief visit to Beirut.
"We condemn it. I condemn it and he (Prodi) condemns this act. We see that it cannot help the peace process," Hariri said.
Prodi added: "I have made the same declaration to (Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin) Netanyahu. This is taking us backwards instead of moving closer to peace."
Israeli bulldozers started on Tuesday breaking ground for the 6,500 housing units at Jabal Abu Ghneim, despite worldwide criticism and fears of Palestinian violence.
The Italian Prime Minister, who arrived in Beirut earlier in the day from Damascus, said Italy remained committed to assisting Lebanon in its post-civil war reconstruction projects.
"Italy will help your initiatives to finish reconstruction of all basic structures that your country needs, water, sewage, communications, bridges and damns," he said.
Italy is Lebanon's biggest trading partner and is one of the biggest financial contributors to the rebuilding effort. Major Italian firms, like Ansaldo, are involved in the reconstruction works.
Hariri said an agreement related to financial aid and assistance through a series of projects was being finalised between the two countries.
He did not give further details but an official source said the project was a "serious multi-million one".

"Two protocols will be signed in relation to avoiding dual taxation and giving insurance to investors. The third agreement related to financial assistance is being prepared with specific projects for specific amounts," he said.
Prodi said Italy was ready to make concrete initiatives to help Lebanon's industrial sector.

"We want Italy to give its help and presence for the reconstruction of the Lebanese industry...There is room for cooperation with small and medium-sized Lebanese companies. We will put forward concrete initiatives," he said.
